note: Research snapshot of the table 6 professional designated services as summarised in AUSTRAC's official guidance, scoped to services an Australian legal practice can trigger. Item wording here is AUSTRAC's overview, not the statutory text: verify the Act text through $check-commonwealth-legislation before reliance. A service matching no entry is 'cannot be determined', never 'not designated'.

statutory_basis.act: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth), subsection 6(5B) table 6, as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Amendment Act 2024 (Cth)
statutory_basis.commencement: Obligations for table 6 services apply from 1 July 2026
statutory_basis.review_note: At the 24 September 2026 review AUSTRAC's pages could not be reached, so guidance_last_updated was not reconfirmed; record the guidance page's current last-updated date at use

items.summary: Assisting in the planning or execution of a transaction, or otherwise acting for or on behalf of a person in a transaction, to sell, buy or transfer real estate
legal_practice_examples: property transaction advice that directly advances the sale, purchase or transfer
scope_notes: carve-out for services pursuant to or resulting from a court or tribunal order

items.summary: Assisting in the planning or execution of a transaction, or otherwise acting for or on behalf of a person in a transaction, to sell, buy or transfer a body corporate or legal arrangement
legal_practice_examples: share or business sale and purchase work
transfers of trusts or other legal arrangements
scope_notes: carve-out for services pursuant to or resulting from a court or tribunal order

items.summary: Receiving, holding, controlling or managing a person's property to help in the planning or execution of a transaction
legal_practice_examples: holding transaction funds or property in the practice trust account as part of a transaction
scope_notes: subsection 6(5C) incidental trust-money exemption may apply where the practice provides no other designated service and money is held for payments reasonably incidental to a non-designated service; the exemption operates at whole-of-practice level
the trust-account counterparty is not the customer — the customer is the client identified in the customer column

items.summary: Assisting in organising, planning or executing a transaction for equity or debt financing relating to a body corporate or legal arrangement (or proposed body corporate or legal arrangement)
legal_practice_examples: acting on capital raisings, loan and security transactions for corporate clients

items.summary: Selling or transferring a shelf company
Assisting in the planning or execution of the creation or restructuring of a body corporate or legal arrangement
legal_practice_examples: drafting and facilitating execution of trust deeds
scope_notes: advice about an existing body corporate or legal arrangement, after the event, is generally not within the item

items.summary: Acting on behalf of a person in particular positions in a body corporate or legal arrangement
legal_practice_examples: practitioners acting as nominee director, secretary, trustee or in equivalent positions for clients
scope_notes: items 7 and 8 are summarised together in AUSTRAC's overview; verify the exact statutory position lists in the Act text

items.summary: Arranging for another person to act in particular positions in a body corporate or legal arrangement
legal_practice_examples: arranging nominee officers or trustees for clients
scope_notes: items 7 and 8 are summarised together in AUSTRAC's overview; verify the exact statutory position lists in the Act text

items.summary: Providing a registered office address or principal place of business address for a body corporate or legal arrangement
legal_practice_examples: practice address used as clients' registered office

common_elements.sufficiently_linked: Assistance is regulated only when sufficiently linked to the outcome: it must directly advance the transaction, creation or restructure. Merely influencing how a client proceeds, general legal advice or ancillary services is not a designated service.
common_elements.course_of_business: The service must be provided in the course of carrying on a business; it need not be the principal activity and pro bono provision does not exclude it.
common_elements.external_customer: The customer must be external to the practice and its business group; in-house counsel advising only their employer are generally not providing designated services.
common_elements.geographical_link: Obligations require a geographical link to Australia — a separate check for cross-border services: https://www.austrac.gov.au/new-austrac/geographical-link-requirement
common_elements.standing_exemptions: Exemptions exist including for legal aid commissions, community legal centres and barristers acting for Australian government bodies — verify at https://www.austrac.gov.au/node/139 and against the Act and Rules
